LESSON: OBLIQUE PROJECTION

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: PRE-TECHNICAL STUDIES
Strand: Communication in Pre-Technical Studies
Topic 2.1: Oblique Projection
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 14

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Oblique Projection, part of Communication in Pre-Technical Studies in Grade 9 PRE-TECHNICAL STUDIES.

Key inquiry question: How are oblique drawings used in technical fields?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. use print or digital media to search for information on the characteristic of oblique drawings,

2. brainstorm on the characteristic of oblique drawings,

3. discuss the steps for drawing shaped blocks in oblique projection,

4. draw given drawings in oblique projection without using instruments (cavalier and cabinet),

5. use geometrical set drawing instruments to draw shaped blocks in oblique projection (cabinet),

6. walk around the locality to observe the use of oblique drawings.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. use print or digital media to search for information on the characteristic of oblique drawings,
2. brainstorm on the characteristic of oblique drawings,
3. discuss the steps for drawing shaped blocks in oblique projection,
4. draw given drawings in oblique projection without using instruments (cavalier and cabinet),
5. use geometrical set drawing instruments to draw shaped blocks in oblique projection (cabinet),
6. walk around the locality to observe the use of oblique drawings.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Oblique Projection together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and Collaboration: learner develops speaking, listening and self-expression skills when brainstorming on

the characteristic of oblique drawings.

• Critical Thinking and Problem Solving: learner develops interpretation and inference skills when drawing oblique

diagrams.

Values:
• Responsibility: learner cares for drawing instruments when drawing three dimensional objects in oblique projection.

• Unity: learner cooperates with others when using digital devices to search for information on the characteristics of oblique

drawings.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Social Cohesion: learner develops ability to relate well with others as they brainstorm on the characteristics of oblique

drawings.

Link to other Subjects:

Mathematics: learner enhances skills of solid geometry when drawing oblique diagrams.
